were prepared by the arc-melting of the mixture of the constituent elements with a purity higher than 99.95 % under an argon atmosphere. After remelting at least five times to achieve compositional homogeneity, the master alloy ingot was cut into small pieces (each about 75 g), which were further remelted and drop-cast into a water-cooled copper mold (15 mm × 15 mm × 50 mm), respectively.
The ingots were then cold rolled with multiple passes, with the thickness down to 6 mm, followed by annealing at different temperatures for 1 h and subsequently quenched in water.

mechanisms.name: chemical fluctuation-induced soft and hard domain formation

evidence.quote: Such superior mechanical performance originates from dual-scale chemical fluctuations (M-CFs and L-CFs), which induce heterogeneous local environments that govern dislocation behavior.

regions enriched with Ti and Zr are more prone to atomic movement during the deformation, acting as "soft zones" in dislocation motion. On the other hand, those regions enriched with Nb, Ta, and Mo act as "hard zones," serving as obstacles for dislocation movements.
This soft-hard interplay, confirmed by bond-order analyses and stacking fault energy calculations, effectively balances strength and ductility.
More importantly, the dislocation loops, frequent cross-slips, as well as planar slips with the extraordinary pinning effect of the dislocation, have been widely observed in TZN-740
the increased cross-slip of dislocations because low yusf often leads to a wider spread dislocation, requiring more energy to achieve cross-slip
As revealed by STEM images, multiple slip systems are activated in TZN-740.
the activation of multiple slip systems, alleviating excessive dislocation pile-up on specific slip planes, and thus improving the deformation coordination.
Zr-enriched regions act as “ soft ” domains, lowering the energy barrier for dislocation motion and providing preferential slip pathways
while Nb-, Ta-, and/or Mo-enriched regions serve as “ hard ” domains, elevating unstable stacking fault energies ( yusf ) to impede dislocation glide and promote cross-slip.
This soft-hard interplay, confirmed by bond-order analyses and stacking fault energy calculations, effectively balances strength and ductility.
